rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty builder trees go (a row of jacarandas, magnolias, eucalyptus and ficus along the back fences, two norfolk pines and a magnolia 3 m from the house fronts, others in the south yards); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the grill, two swing sets, two adirondack chairs and on the open south lot corner.

trees.why: the back yard with the kettle grill (1.4 m off): a coral tree over the cook
the back yard with the swing set (2.6 m off), 5.7 m from the house: shade over the swings
the south yard with the adirondack chair: a magnolia to sit under
the east yard's adirondack chair, 37 m on: the same, the street's second yard tree
the south-west yard with the swing set (2.8 m off): shade over the swings
the open lot corner at the south, 24 m from the walls: an old ficus where there is room for it
